cloudContinuity.scope: Native phone → tablet organization order, offline tablet drags/relaunch → reconnect → phone return; two projects/sections/filters/favorites. Mac authenticated transport reads final data. Seeded disposable fixture; all reorder actions use native UI.
cloudContinuity.offlineBoundary: Exactly eight PATCH mutations contain only order_index. Tablet cache retains new order after relaunch while authenticated server reads retain the phone order. Reconnect drains queue; phone receives the returned order with all original IDs and non-order metadata unchanged.
cloudContinuity.earlierAttempts: Composed checkpoints, not a fresh all-green nine-phase driver. The first phone drag opened the row context menu because the button frame excluded the handle. The first tablet drag used a percentage that landed left of the handle on a wide row and scrolled instead. Actual recordings were inspected; server/cache inspection confirmed no reorder/pending work at either failure. Corrected gestures use the cell trailing edge. Resumed from phone-reorder, then tablet-offline, retaining completed phases and the original server baseline. No backend reordering was used to make tests pass.
cloudContinuity.productionChange: Stable row accessibility identifiers distinguish favorite, project, filter and section entries in each independently owned app. Ordering behavior itself was committed previously.
